title: cocoon
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A single-volume war drama based on the true story of the Himeyuri corps of student nurses in Okinawa in the Second World War. Schoolgirls San and Mayu are drafted as assistant nurses and sent to work in cave field hospitals, where classmates die from bombing, starvation and disease. When the girls are told to make their own way home across the battlefield, they flee along the shoreline with no food, medicine or defense (VIZ blurb via AniList; Comics Beat).
life_message: Friendship and the will to live are precious, and war cannot justify what it does to the young.

content.note: Exploded girls, blood, maggots, burning, body fragments, amputation and a mass grave (Comics Beat); Gore and Brutality tags (AniList, MU).
Starvation, constant death of classmates and flight through combat zones (VIZ blurb, Comics Beat; AniList Tragedy, Survival).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Girls' lives valued in themselves; no honor code celebrated (Comics Beat).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Wartime orders shown as harmful, but no freedom ideal stated.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Bonds among classmates rather than family (VIZ blurb: San and best friend Mayu).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Military authority that recruits and abandons the girls is critiqued (review: atrocities unjustified).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Historical, non-religious framing of the Himeyuri story.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Starvation and flight make survival the overriding concern (VIZ blurb).

folkways.japan: Draws on Okinawa's memory of the Battle of Okinawa and the Himeyuri students, a major subject of Japanese and Okinawan war remembrance.

delivery.evidence: Comics Beat reads it as anti-war, strongest on personal experience, with some passages 'hamfisted'; one review only.
delivery.note: The anti-war view is carried mainly by what happens to the girls; the militarist view is not argued on its own terms (to verify).

winners_losers: No side wins; the girls lose classmates and childhood, and sympathy rests entirely with them against the war that used them.
